I farm only 1.1 mu, so I count every bag of fertilizer and every trip for water. I have done wheat-maize for many years, so I will not change the pattern. I finished middle school, so I do look at what the dealer says and what people around me plant, but I still trust what has worked on our land. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, and give enough water because I have a well and wheat here cannot rely on the sky. I will put more money into wheat and maize fertilizer than gamble on cutting it too low. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives better yield around here, and I will keep the field turning fast so I do not lose the season. My land is small, labor is mainly family labor, and some people work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple: stable seed, enough fertilizer, 2 to 3 irrigations where needed, and pesticide only when I see pressure building. I will follow roughly what has worked in recent years in our area, not do anything fancy, and aim first at not losing yield.
